title: A fridge at the end of the world
text: Halfway between mainland Norway and the North Pole, a concrete doorway {{1}} into a mountainside. Inside lies the Svalbard Global Seed Vault: a long tunnel, three cold chambers, and more than a million seed samples from nearly every country on Earth. The idea is a backup for the backups. National seed banks — the gene banks that {{2}} crop varieties for plant breeders — can be destroyed by war, flood or a simple failure of funding; the vault is designed to {{3}} all of them at once, storing copies in permafrost conditions that need no power to stay cold. Seeds {{4}} there are packed in foil, catalogued and owned by the country that sent them: the vault stores, it does not research. It has already {{5}} its purpose. Seed banks in Syria and the Philippines, damaged by war and typhoon, have withdrawn their {{6}} copies and rebuilt at home. The vault even endured a {{7}} of the conditions it was built for: in 2017, unusually warm weather melted permafrost around the entrance and water seeped into the tunnel — no seeds were harmed, but the design has since been {{8}}. Even a fallback, it turns out, needs a fallback.

gaps.explanation: 'a doorway gapes into a mountainside' — stands wide open; graze = feed or scrape, glow = shine.
'gene banks that maintain crop varieties' — keep them alive and available; manifest = show plainly.
'designed to duplicate all of them at once' — hold copies of every collection; dominate = control.
'seeds stored there are packed in foil' — kept there deliberately; sort = arrange by type, stamp = mark with a seal.
'has already served its purpose' — the fixed idiom; deserve = merit, reserve = keep for later.
'withdrawn their deposited copies' — the copies they had placed in the vault; depose = remove from office, deplete = use up.
'endured a breach of the conditions it was built for' — a breaking through; brooch = an ornamental pin.
'the design has since been reinforced' — strengthened; reimburse = pay back, revoke = cancel.
